# Fixtures

Test data for the `nf-agents` crates. Everything here is **synthetic**: three words of seed
text pushed through a toy pipeline. No real, genomic or patient data. Licensed Apache-2.0 like
the rest of the repository.

**Generated files: never edit by hand.** Regenerate them with the script below instead; a
hand edit breaks the manifest hashes (CI fails) or, worse, silently drifts from what Nextflow
really writes.

## Layout

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `pipelines/minimal/` | The pipeline: `GENERATE -> TRANSFORM -> SUMMARIZE`, a `greeting` param, an `output` block publishing `upper/upper.txt` and `summary.txt` (label `summary`). |
| `lineage/<version>/` | One version dir per Nextflow release (`25.04.8`, `25.10.9`, `26.04.9`, `26.10.7`). |

Each version dir holds two runs (`--greeting hello` = `RUN1`, `--greeting bonjour` = `RUN2`):

| Entry | What |
| --- | --- |
| `.lineage/` | The lineage store exactly as Nextflow wrote it. |
| `work/…`, `results-*/…` | Every data file (the `path` of a `FileOutput` record), as a regular file. Published symlinks are dereferenced; nothing else from `work/` is kept. |
| `nextflow.config` | The config the runs used (`lineage.enabled = true`). |
| `oracle/` | `nextflow lineage …` output per case: `<case>.args` (JSON argv after `nextflow`), `.out`, `.err` (byte-exact), `.exit`; `ids.json` maps `RUN1`, `RUN2`, `TASK_<PROCESS>_RUN<n>` to LIDs. `check-tampered` and `check-mtime-only` ran on a throw-away copy. |
| `manifest.json` | Provenance and the mtime manifest (below). |

## Provenance

Generated by `scripts/gen-fixtures.sh` in the official `nextflow/nextflow:<version>` images; the
exact image tag and digest is the `image` field of each `manifest.json`. The tree is mounted at
the fixed recorded root `/nf-agents-fixture` and runs with `--cpus 2` as the image's default
user, so records hold no host path, user or host name (`config.poolSize` is `2`). LIDs, session
IDs, run names and timestamps change on every regeneration: tests must read them from
`oracle/ids.json`, never hard-code them.

## mtime manifest

`nextflow lineage check` hashes a file's recorded path, size and **mtime**. git does not keep
mtimes, so `manifest.json` lists every data file as `{path, size, mtime_ms, sha256}` (`path`
relative to the version dir, sorted; `mtime_ms` in milliseconds since the epoch). To make
`check` succeed on a checkout: copy the version dir, set each file's mtime to `mtime_ms`, and
mount the copy at `/nf-agents-fixture`:

```bash
cp -r fixtures/lineage/26.10.7 /tmp/fx
python3 scripts/fixtures/restore_mtimes.py /tmp/fx
docker run --rm -v /tmp/fx:/nf-agents-fixture -w /nf-agents-fixture \
  nextflow/nextflow:26.10.7 nextflow lineage check "$(python3 -c \
  'import json; print(json.load(open("/tmp/fx/oracle/ids.json"))["RUN1"])')/summary.txt"
```

In Rust, `std::fs::File::set_modified(UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_millis(mtime_ms))` does the same.

## Regenerate

Needs bash and Docker only (no Nextflow, Python or Java on the host):

```bash
scripts/gen-fixtures.sh                 # all core versions into fixtures/lineage
scripts/gen-fixtures.sh 26.10.7         # one version
scripts/gen-fixtures.sh --verify        # re-check the committed dirs, no regeneration
scripts/gen-fixtures.sh --out "$(mktemp -d)" 26.11.0-edge
```

A version dir is replaced only after its generation, a round trip (plain copy without mtimes
-> `check` fails; restore mtimes -> `check` of every `FileOutput` succeeds and `list` equals
the oracle) and the offline check all passed. CI runs the offline part on every PR:

```bash
python3 -I -m unittest discover -s scripts/fixtures -p 'test_*.py'
python3 -I scripts/fixtures/check.py fixtures/lineage
```
